_comment: Values follow the NASA Planetary Fact Sheets (nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet). Rotation periods are positive magnitudes; retrograde spin is expressed by an axial tilt above 90 degrees. Keys starting with _ are ignored by the API.

bodies.name: Sun
bodies.summary: The Sun is the star at the centre of our solar system. Its gravity holds every planet in orbit and its light powers life on Earth.
_todo: TODO verify: the Sun has no parent, so distanceFromParentMillionKm and orbitalPeriodDays are 0 by convention
TODO verify: rotationPeriodHours 609.12 is the sidereal period near the equator; the Sun rotates more slowly at the poles

bodies.name: Mercury
bodies.summary: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun. It has almost no atmosphere, so its surface swings between scorching days and freezing nights.

bodies.name: Venus
bodies.summary: Venus is nearly the same size as Earth but is wrapped in thick clouds that trap heat, making it the hottest planet. It spins backwards compared with most planets.

bodies.name: Earth
bodies.summary: Earth is our home and the only world known to support life. Liquid water covers about 71 percent of its surface.

bodies.name: Mars
bodies.summary: Mars is a cold desert world coloured red by rusty dust. Robots have explored its surface for decades, searching for signs of ancient water and life.

bodies.name: Jupiter
bodies.summary: Jupiter is the largest planet, a gas giant more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined. Its Great Red Spot is a storm wider than Earth.

bodies.name: Saturn
bodies.summary: Saturn is a gas giant famous for its bright, wide rings made of ice and rock. It is the second-largest planet in the solar system.
_todo: TODO verify: distanceFromParentMillionKm differs between fact sheet revisions (1432.0 vs 1433.5)

bodies.name: Uranus
bodies.summary: Uranus is an ice giant that is tipped over so far it rolls around the Sun on its side. Methane in its atmosphere gives it a pale blue-green colour.
_todo: TODO verify: distanceFromParentMillionKm differs between fact sheet revisions (2867.0 vs 2872.5)

bodies.name: Neptune
bodies.summary: Neptune is the most distant planet, a dark, cold ice giant with the fastest winds in the solar system. One trip around the Sun takes it about 165 Earth years.
_todo: TODO verify: distanceFromParentMillionKm differs between fact sheet revisions (4515.0 vs 4495.1)

bodies.name: Pluto
bodies.summary: Pluto is a small, icy dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt. NASA's New Horizons spacecraft flew past it in 2015 and found mountains of ice and a heart-shaped plain.
_todo: TODO verify: axialTiltDeg is quoted as 122.53 (to its orbit) or 119.5 depending on the source

bodies.name: Moon
bodies.summary: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite, a grey, cratered world with no air to breathe. Twelve astronauts walked on it during the Apollo missions.
_todo: TODO verify: axialTiltDeg 6.68 is measured against the Moon's orbit around Earth; against the ecliptic it is about 1.54
